excerpt: \captionof{figure}{End-to-end architecture and tensor flow of the MobilePIXORNeXt LiDAR object detector. Unordered 3D LiDAR point clouds are transformed via the parameter-free Strata-BEV14 rasterizer into a 14-channel statistical BEV tensor   without learned pillar encoders. The streamlined backbone extracts multi-scale features through ConvNeXt-style stages with embedded parameter-free Block-SimAM attention, fused by a top-down Scale-Gated Feature Pyramid Network (SG-FPN) into a 32-channel shared representation at stride 4 ( ). Decoupled GroupedHeader towers process Car and Pedestrian/Cyclist categories independently. Solid arrows trace the feedforward inference path, whereas dashed arrows indicate training-only supervision incorporating Oriented Geometric Alignment (OGA), IoU-Aware Quality Alignment (IQA), and dynamic loss balancing via Temperature-Softmax Bounded Uncertainty Weighting (T-SBUW).}

Conventional backbones with small   convolutions require excessive network depth to cover the requisite spatial context, ballooning latency and parameter count. In contrast, at our input grid resolution of  \,m, a single   depthwise receptive field directly spans  \,m of physical terrain at stride 1, and rapidly expands to over  \,m by Stage 3 (stride 8)---sufficient to envelop an entire passenger vehicle in a single layer without dilation artifacts. To achieve this wide context under strict parameter parsimony, we design the \textbf{MobilePixorNeXt Backbone} hierarchy featuring large   depthwise convolutions, inverted bottleneck expansions, and LayerScale residual stabilization organized into repeated \texttt{MobilePixorNeXt-S} blocks.

excerpt: In autonomous driving perception, detecting small, non-rigid objects such as pedestrians presents the most challenging operational regime due to extreme point sparsity and severe aspect-ratio disparity. As evidenced in Table~  and the Precision--Recall curves in Figure~ , MobilePIXORNeXt achieved \textbf{60.75\% Moderate AP} on Pedestrians, outperforming PointPillars ( , a   gain) and SECOND ( , a   gain), while more than doubling the baseline MobilePIXOR ( , a   gain). We attribute this performance advantage primarily to two architectural mechanisms: (i) Strata-BEV14's continuous subcell displacement offsets  , which mitigate the   grid quantization error that inherently impairs small object localization; and (ii) the decoupled GroupedHeader architecture, which isolates pedestrian regression from large vehicle footprints to alleviate gradient interference across morphologically disparate categories.

excerpt: The empirical results indicate that high-accuracy 3D LiDAR object detection does not strictly necessitate parameter-heavy point-cloud encoders or computationally demanding 3D sparse convolutions. By enriching the deterministic 2D BEV representation with multi-band vertical densities, elevation dispersion moments, and continuous subcell centroid displacements, a streamlined ConvNeXt-style 2D convolutional network extracts expressive geometric features with fewer than   parameters. In addition, enforcing physical realism in data augmentation (\texttt{PC-GTA}) and resolving multi-task gradient competition through decoupled grouped heads provided larger empirical performance gains than model depth scaling alone.
